user.title: How should your bottle's drinks reach Home Assistant?
user.description:
There are three ways. They differ in what you need to install, whether you need a WaterH account, and when drinks show up. You can change the Bluetooth and Android app settings later under **Configure**; switching to or from the WaterH account means adding the integration again.

The first two replace the official WaterH app. Don't use the official app alongside them: it takes the drinks off the bottle when it syncs, and Home Assistant would never see those.

menu_options.cloud: WaterH account (keep using the official app)

menu_option_descriptions.pick_bluetooth: Nothing to install on your phone and no WaterH account; works for iPhone and Android. Home Assistant connects to the bottle itself through a Bluetooth adapter or ESPHome Bluetooth proxy. Drinks sync whenever the bottle is near one; drinks taken away from home stay on the bottle and arrive (with their real times) when you're back. Needs Bluetooth in range of where the bottle usually is.
menu_option_descriptions.local: For Android users who want drinks to show up while away from home. You install the WaterH Sync app (an APK from GitHub, not the Play Store); it reads the bottle on your phone and sends drinks to Home Assistant, over the internet if Home Assistant is reachable remotely. No WaterH account. You can add Bluetooth through Home Assistant later as a second path.
menu_option_descriptions.cloud: For people who want to keep using the official WaterH app. Home Assistant reads your drinks from your WaterH account. Drinks only appear after the official app uploads them, which it only does while it's open. Needs your WaterH email and password.

cloud.title: Sign in to WaterH
cloud.description:
Use the email and password for your WaterH app account. If you signed up with Google or Facebook, set a password first with "Forgot password" in the WaterH app. Your password is only used to get a login token and is not stored.

**Remember:** drinks only reach your WaterH account (and so Home Assistant) when the official WaterH app is open and syncing. If you'd rather not depend on that, go back and choose Bluetooth through Home Assistant.

local.title: WaterH Sync Android app
local.description:
The WaterH Sync app reads drinks from your bottle on your phone and sends them to Home Assistant, where they are stored. Nothing is sent to WaterH, and no WaterH account is needed.

- Install the app from github.com/raymanvh/waterh-sync-android (Android only).
- With a remote URL (Nabu Casa or your own), drinks arrive while you're away from home too. Without one, they wait on the bottle or phone until you're home.
- Stop using the official WaterH app: it would take the drinks off the bottle before the app sees them.
- You can also let Home Assistant sync the bottle over Bluetooth when you're home; turn that on later under Configure.

local_finish.description:
In WaterH Sync, choose **Local only** and paste this URL. Keep it private: anyone who has it can add drinks.

{webhook_url}

You can find it again later under Configure.

To sync while away from home, use your external or Nabu Casa remote URL. Otherwise drinks wait until you're home.

pick_bluetooth.title: Choose your bottle
pick_bluetooth.description:
Home Assistant can hear {count} WaterH bottle(s) right now. Pick yours below.

**Bottle not listed?**
- Pick the bottle up or tilt it to wake it; it only advertises while awake.
- Make sure no phone is connected to it (close the official WaterH app and the WaterH Sync app). A bottle accepts one connection at a time.
- A Bluetooth adapter on Home Assistant, or an ESPHome Bluetooth proxy with active connections enabled, has to be within range (roughly the same room).

Then submit with the box empty to search again. You can also type the bottle's Bluetooth address (AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF).

bluetooth_confirm.title: Bluetooth through Home Assistant
bluetooth_confirm.description:
Bottle: **{bottle}**

**How it works**
- Whenever the bottle is within range of a Bluetooth adapter or proxy, Home Assistant connects to it every {interval} minutes (you can change this under Configure).
- Each sync reads the drinks stored on the bottle, saves them in Home Assistant, and only then clears them from the bottle.
- It also sets the bottle's clock, daily goal and today's total to match Home Assistant, so the bottle's own display agrees with your dashboards. This can be turned off under Configure.
- Battery level and charging are read on every sync.

**Good to know**
- Away from home, the bottle keeps drinks (with their times) until it's back in range. Nothing is lost, it's just delayed. How many drinks the bottle can hold is not known, so don't go weeks without syncing.
- Stop using the official WaterH app: it would take the drinks off the bottle before Home Assistant sees them.
- Drinks are stored only in Home Assistant (the last 30 days). Long-term history lives in Home Assistant's statistics.

init.title: WaterH options

sync.title: Sync settings
sync.description:
Drinks can reach Home Assistant in two ways here, and you can use either or both. A drink seen by both is only counted once.

- **Bluetooth through Home Assistant**: Home Assistant connects to the bottle when it's in range of a Bluetooth adapter or proxy. Choose Off to stop.
- **WaterH Sync Android app**: your phone sends drinks, including while you're away if Home Assistant is reachable remotely. App URL (keep it private):

{webhook_url}

data.update_bottle: Keep the bottle in step with Home Assistant
data.android_app: Accept drinks from the WaterH Sync Android app

data_description.address: The bottle Home Assistant syncs over Bluetooth, or Off.
data_description.sync_interval: How often to sync while the bottle is in range. Shorter means drinks show up sooner but the bottle wakes its radio more often, which uses a little more of its battery. 5 minutes is a good balance. Logging a drink or changing the goal in Home Assistant syncs right away.
data_description.update_bottle: Sets the bottle's clock, daily goal and today's total to Home Assistant's on each sync, so the bottle's display matches your dashboards. Turn off to only read drinks.
data_description.android_app: Turn on if you also use the WaterH Sync app, e.g. to sync while away from home.

menu_option_descriptions.sync: Bluetooth bottle, sync interval, keeping the bottle in step, the Android app, and the volume unit.
menu_option_descriptions.recalibrate: Reset the bottle's empty weight so it measures drinks accurately. Use this if drinks are logged too large or too small.

recalibrate.title: Recalibrate the bottle
recalibrate.description:
The bottle works out how much you drank from changes in what it measures. Recalibrating records what the bottle reads when it's **empty**, as its new starting point. This is the same as **Recalibrate bottle** in the official WaterH app, and it doesn't touch drinks stored on the bottle.

Recalibrate if drinks are logged noticeably too large or too small. Even calibrated, WaterH says the Boost can be up to 20% off.

**Before you start**
1. Empty the bottle. Pour it out with the cap off so the bottle doesn't log it as a drink.
2. Twist the cap back on.
3. Stand the bottle upright on a flat surface, such as a table, and let go of it.
4. Make sure it's near a Bluetooth adapter or proxy and no phone is connected to it.

Tick each box below, then submit. The bottle's blue light flashes while it records its empty weight. This takes about 10 seconds; don't touch the bottle until it's done.

data.cap_on: The cap is twisted back on
data.flat_surface: It's standing upright on a flat surface
data.not_held: Nobody is holding or touching it

error.no_source: Choose a Bluetooth bottle, turn on the Android app, or both; otherwise no drinks can arrive.
error.invalid_address: That isn't a Bluetooth address. It looks like AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF.
error.no_bluetooth: Home Assistant's Bluetooth integration isn't set up. Add a Bluetooth adapter or ESPHome Bluetooth proxy first.
error.confirm_checklist: Tick every box first. If the bottle isn't empty, capped, upright and left alone, it records the wrong starting point and measures drinks wrong.
error.not_loaded: The integration isn't running right now, so it can't reach the bottle. Check that it's loaded, then try again.

abort.recalibrated: Done. The bottle recorded its new empty weight and can be used normally. To check it, drink a measured amount and compare it with what Home Assistant logs.
